name: Seymour R. Cray
summary: American electrical engineer and supercomputer designer known as the father of the supercomputer.

name: John Markoff
summary: New York Times journalist who wrote Cray's obituary.

name: John Rollwagen
summary: Business executive who worked with Cray at Cray Research Inc.

name: William C. Norris
summary: Founder of Engineering Research Associates and Control Data.

name: Steve S. Chen
summary: Computer designer who worked at Cray Research.

name: Geri M. Harrand
summary: Cray's second wife.

name: Control Data Corp.
summary: Computer manufacturer where Cray designed the CDC 6600.

name: Cray Research Inc.
summary: Supercomputer company founded by Cray in 1972.

name: Cray Computer Corp.
summary: Company founded by Cray in 1989 that filed for bankruptcy in 1995.

name: SRC Computers
summary: Company formed by Cray in August 1995.

name: Engineering Research Associates
summary: Minneapolis company doing contract work for the Navy in cryptography.

name: University of Minnesota
summary: University where Cray received bachelor's and master's degrees.

name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
summary: National laboratory that purchased the first Cray 1 computer.

name: IBM
summary: Computer company whose 7094 was outperformed by the CDC 6600.

name: Chippewa Falls
summary: Wisconsin town where Cray was born and relocated his laboratory.

name: Colorado Springs
summary: Colorado city where Cray died and based Cray Computer Corp.

name: CDC 6600
summary: Supercomputer introduced in 1963, the first to be cooled with Freon.

name: Cray 1
summary: Supercomputer sold to Los Alamos in 1976, folded in on itself like a giant C.

name: Cray 2
summary: Supercomputer finished in 1985 using Flourinert cooling.

name: CDC 1604
summary: First commercial computer to replace vacuum tubes with individual transistors.
